national/agency: Texas has no dual agency. A broker on both sides must be an INTERMEDIARY with written consent, and may appoint an associate to each party (Occ. Code 1101.559-1101.561).
Since January 1, 2026, a written buyer agreement is required before showing a home to a buyer the license holder works for (1101.563).
national/contracts: License holders must use TREC-promulgated forms; a lease longer than one year and any real estate sale must be in writing (Occ. Code 1101.155; Bus. & Com. Code 26.01).
national/disclosures: One-unit residential sellers give the Seller's Disclosure Notice on or before the contract's effective date, or the buyer may terminate within seven days of getting it (Property Code 5.008).
No duty to disclose a death by natural causes, suicide, or accident unrelated to the property's condition, or HIV/AIDS (Occ. Code 1101.556).
national/financing: Texas uses the deed of trust and nonjudicial foreclosure: sale on the first Tuesday of the month, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., at the courthouse, after 21 days' notice and, for a residence, at least 20 days to cure (Property Code 51.002).
national/ownership: Texas IS a community property state. Separate property is what a spouse owned before marriage or received by gift, devise, or descent; everything else acquired during marriage is presumed community (Family Code 3.001-3.003).
Homestead: up to 10 urban acres; up to 200 rural acres for a family or 100 for a single adult (Property Code 41.002).
national/practice: Trust money goes into the broker's trust account by the close of business of the second working day; sales agents never hold it (TREC rule 535.146).
Ads must show the broker's name at least half the size of the largest sales agent contact information (TREC rule 535.155).
national/transfer: An unrecorded conveyance is void against a creditor or later buyer for value without notice; a recorded one is notice to everyone (Property Code 13.001-13.002).
When an offer is signed, the license holder must advise the buyer in writing to have the abstract examined by an attorney or get a title policy (Occ. Code 1101.555).

examples.s: A broker receives earnest money on Friday. Monday is a working day; no written agreement says otherwise.
w: Count working days: Monday is the first, Tuesday the second.
The deadline is the close of business on Tuesday.

tx/conduct.label: Standards of conduct

choices: Is fine if the seller agrees
check.q: A listing agreement without a definite termination date:

choices: No consent if listed in MLS
check.q: Placing a For Sale sign requires:

l: Acts negligently or incompetently, or dishonestly or in bad faith.
Misrepresents, or FAILS TO DISCLOSE, a known significant defect to a potential buyer, including a latent structural defect.
Fails to make clear to all parties which party they are acting for.
Takes pay from more than one party without the full knowledge and consent of all parties.
Commingles another person's money with their own, or fails to account for it.
Splits a fee with anyone other than a license holder or an out-of-state broker or agent.
Signs a services contract with no definite termination date (property management excepted).
Accepts an undisclosed commission, rebate, or profit on a principal's expenditure.
Guarantees future profits from a resale, or sells by lottery or deceptive practice.
Puts a sign on property without the owner's written consent.
Induces a party to break a contract to substitute a new one, or negotiates with someone under an exclusive agreement with another broker.
Publishes misleading advertising, or advertising without the broker's name.
Discriminates on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, disability, familial status, national origin, or ancestry.
Fails to sign a written agreement with a prospective buyer when 1101.563 requires one.
p: TREC may suspend or revoke a license if, while doing brokerage, the license holder:

choices: Allowed only with an attorney present
check.q: A sales agent filling in a TREC-promulgated contract is:

p: A license holder who is not a Texas attorney may not draft an instrument that transfers or affects an interest in real property (other than filling in TREC-adopted forms), and may not advise anyone on the validity or legal sufficiency of an instrument or of title. Doing so means mandatory suspension or revocation. Completing a promulgated form incidental to brokerage is NOT the practice of law.

choices: Deliver it immediately to the sponsoring broker
Deposit it in the agent's own trust account
check.q: A sales agent receives an earnest money check. The agent must:
check.why: Sales agents may not maintain trust accounts.

choices: Close of business on the second working day after receipt
check.q: Trust money must be deposited by:
check.why: Unless the principals agree otherwise in writing.

l: Trust money includes earnest money, rent, security deposits, unearned fees, or any money held for another.
A SALES AGENT may not keep a trust account; trust money must go IMMEDIATELY to the sponsoring broker.

The broker deposits it in a trust account or delivers it to an authorized escrow agent by the close of business of the SECOND WORKING DAY after receiving it, unless the principals agree otherwise in writing.
No commingling, and never in a personal account. A broker may keep a reasonable amount of own money in the account to cover bank fees.
After a written demand, pay out within a reasonable time, which TREC defines as not later than the 30th day.
Keep trust-account records for FOUR YEARS.

check.q: A sales agent can be paid a commission by:

l: A broker may compensate for brokerage only a license holder, or a broker licensed in another state who does none of the negotiating in Texas (1101.651(a)).
A sales agent may accept pay only from the sponsoring broker, and may pay a commission only through that broker (1101.651(b)-(c)).
A license holder may not take a commission, rebate, or fee from a non-client without first disclosing it to the client and getting consent (rule 535.148(a)).
Referral fees to or from other settlement service providers - inspectors, lenders, mortgage brokers, title companies - are prohibited (rule 535.148(d)).

choices: The same size as the agent's name
Half the size of the largest sales agent contact information
Any size, as long as present
check.q: The broker's name in an ad must be at least:

l: Every advertisement must show the name of the license holder or team placing it AND the BROKER's name in at least HALF THE SIZE of the largest contact information for any sales agent.
On social media or text, the required information may be one direct link away if it is readily noticeable there.
A team name that implies an independent brokerage ("brokerage", "company", "associates") is misleading.

Each business website's homepage needs a readily noticeable link labelled "Texas Real Estate Commission Information About Brokerage Services" (10-point font or larger) or "TREC Information About Brokerage Services" (12-point or larger).

check.q: An unlicensed assistant may:
check.why: Providing access is showing, and showing needs a license.

p: Showing a property needs a license - that includes unlocking or providing access for a prospect and hosting an open house (rule 535.4(c)). TREC's guidance: unlicensed assistants may do clerical work, schedule showings, and confirm information already advertised such as size or price. They may not solicit, show, host open houses, review contracts or facilitate the deal, or move trust money.

tx/conduct.summary: The Act lists what gets a license suspended or revoked, and TREC's rules fill in trust money and advertising. The exam favours specific numbers (two working days, four years, half the size) and the practices that are flatly prohibited: commingling, paying unlicensed people, undisclosed fees, and drafting legal documents.
traps: Sales agents NEVER hold trust money - straight to the broker.
Two WORKING days, not calendar days, and only unless the principals agree otherwise in writing.
Records are kept four years.
Half the size of the largest SALES AGENT contact info - the broker's name, not the team's.
Filling in TREC forms is not practising law; drafting a deed is.
Fees to unlicensed people for brokerage are prohibited, and referral fees from lenders, inspectors or title companies are too.
vocab: Mixing trust money with the license holder's own money.
Earnest money, rent, deposits, unearned fees, or any money held for another.
Money returned to a party; must be disclosed to the client and consented to.
Information About Brokerage Services, the TREC notice.
Drafting real property instruments or advising on title or legal sufficiency.

tx/contracts.blurb: Promulgated forms, statute of frauds, seller's disclosure notice.

examples.k: The buyer has until June 17 to terminate.
examples.s: Contract effective June 1. Seller delivers the disclosure notice June 10.
w: It was due on or before June 1.
The buyer may terminate for any reason within seven days of receiving it.

tx/contracts.label: Contracts & disclosures

choices: The buyer is from out of state
The owner's attorney prepared it and the owner requires it
check.q: A license holder may use a non-TREC contract when:

p: TREC may require license holders to use contract forms prepared by the Texas Real Estate Broker-Lawyer Committee and adopted by TREC (1101.155). Failing to use a required form is grounds for discipline (1101.652(a-1)(3)). A license holder may still use a form prepared by the property owner, or prepared by an attorney and required by the owner. TREC-adopted listing forms must say commissions are negotiable.

check.q: Which must be in writing to be enforceable?

l: A contract for the sale of real estate.
A lease of real estate for longer than ONE YEAR.
An agreement that cannot be performed within one year.
A promise to answer for another's debt.
And separately, a commission agreement for selling or buying real estate (Occ. Code 1101.806).
p: These must be in writing and signed by the person to be charged:

choices: May terminate for any reason within seven days after receiving it
check.q: The buyer received the seller's disclosure two days after signing the contract. The buyer:

choices: An owner selling the house they have lived in
An executor selling for an estate
check.q: Which sale needs a seller's disclosure notice?
check.why: Fiduciary and foreclosure transfers are exempt.

l: A seller of residential property of not more than ONE dwelling unit must give the buyer a written disclosure notice.
It is given on or before the EFFECTIVE DATE of the contract. If it is not, the buyer may terminate for ANY reason within SEVEN DAYS after receiving it.
Completed to the seller's best knowledge; marking an item unknown complies.
No duty to disclose deaths by natural causes, suicide, or accident unrelated to the property's condition, or that an occupant had AIDS or HIV (also 1101.556).

Exempt transfers include court-ordered and foreclosure sales, transfers by a bankruptcy trustee, by a fiduciary of an estate or trust, between co-owners, to a spouse or lineal relative, in a divorce, to or from a governmental entity, and a new home never occupied.

check.q: Failing to give the written abstract/title advice can cost the agent:

p: When an offer is signed, the license holder must advise each buyer IN WRITING to have the abstract examined by an attorney of the buyer's choosing OR to be provided with or obtain a title insurance policy. A license holder who fails to may not receive the commission (1101.806(d)).

tx/contracts.summary: Texas license holders must use TREC's promulgated forms, real estate contracts must be in writing, and a home seller owes the buyer a written disclosure notice before the contract - or the buyer gets seven days to walk away.
traps: Disclosure notice: on or before the effective date; late = 7-day walk-away right for ANY reason.
It applies to one dwelling unit residential property; duplexes and up are outside 5.008(a).
Lease over ONE year needs writing; one year or less does not.
Abstract-or-title advice is IN WRITING, and missing it forfeits the commission.
vocab: A contract form TREC adopted and requires license holders to use.
The committee that drafts TREC's forms.
The rule that certain agreements must be written and signed.
Property Code 5.008 condition notice for one-unit homes.
The history of recorded documents; an attorney should examine it.

tx/licensing.blurb: Who needs a license, exemptions, education, renewal, inactive status.

examples.k: Renew now for 1.5x. At day 91 it becomes 2x; at six months it cannot be renewed at all.
examples.s: A sales agent's license expired 75 days ago.
w: 90 days or less late is the first tier.
The fee is 1-1/2 times the renewal fee.

tx/licensing.label: Licensing

choices: For another person, for or expecting compensation
check.q: The definition of broker turns on acting:
check.why: Leasing and procuring prospects count too.

p: A broker is a person who, for a commission or other valuable consideration, or expecting one, does an act like selling, buying, leasing, listing, negotiating, auctioning, or procuring prospects for real estate FOR ANOTHER PERSON (1101.002(1)).

check.q: An attorney-in-fact is exempt for up to how many transactions a year?

choices: A friend who finds buyers for others in exchange for a fee
An owner leasing the owner's own house
check.q: Which person needs a license?
check.why: Procuring prospects for a fee is brokerage.

l: An attorney licensed in Texas.
An attorney-in-fact under a power of attorney for NOT MORE THAN THREE transactions a year.
A public official doing official duties.
A licensed auctioneer selling real estate at auction who does no other act of a broker.
A person acting under a court order, a will, or a written trust.
An owner's employee selling structures the owner built in the owner's business.
An on-site apartment manager.
An owner, or the owner's employee, leasing the owner's own property.
Mineral, timber or energy interests; cemetery lots; leasing or managing a hotel or motel; and a foreclosure sale under a deed of trust.
p: The Act does not apply to:

choices: Discloses the equitable interest in writing
Assigns no more than three a year
check.q: Assigning a purchase contract without a license is allowed if the person:
check.why: No written disclosure means it is brokerage.

p: Someone may sell an option or assign a purchase contract without a license only if they do not use it to engage in brokerage AND they disclose IN WRITING the nature of their equitable interest to any seller or potential buyer. Without that written disclosure it IS brokerage (1101.0045).

check.q: Qualifying education for a sales agent license is:

choices: Four years in the preceding 60 months
Two years in the preceding 36 months
check.q: A broker applicant needs active experience of:

l: Be at least 18, and a U.S. citizen or lawfully admitted alien (1101.354).
Satisfy TREC as to honesty, trustworthiness and integrity, and pass the exam.
Sales agent: 12 semester hours of qualifying courses, which the handbook lists as 180 classroom hours (1101.358).
A sales agent must be sponsored by a licensed broker to act; when sponsorship ends the license goes INACTIVE (1101.367).
Broker: at least FOUR years of active experience in the 60 months before applying, qualifying courses up to 60 semester hours, and the broker responsibility course (1101.356).
Exam retakes: three attempts; after three failures you need 30 more hours if you failed one portion, 60 if you failed both (handbook).

check.q: A license expired 4 months ago can be renewed for:
check.why: Over 90 days but under six months.

check.q: Continuing education after the first renewal is at least:

l: Licenses run 24 MONTHS (1101.451).
First renewal of a sales agent license: 18 semester hours of courses (SAE). TREC may NOT waive it (1101.454).
After that: at least 15 classroom hours of CE per license term, at least 8 of them on legal topics such as TREC rules, fair housing, and Property Code issues (1101.455).
Expired 90 days or less: renew for 1.5 times the fee. More than 90 days but under six months: 2 times. Six months or longer: cannot renew; start over as a new applicant (1101.451).
Brokers keep a fixed office in Texas, and apply for a new license within 10 days of moving it (1101.552).
When a sales agent and sponsoring broker part, the one ending it must immediately notify the other AND TREC in writing; a new sponsoring broker can reactivate the license (1101.367).

tx/licensing.summary: Anyone who, for a fee or the expectation of one, does brokerage for another needs a license unless an exemption applies. Learn the exemption list, the eligibility basics, and the renewal numbers: 12 hours to get in, 18 for the first renewal, 15 CE after that, 24-month licenses.
traps: 12 hours to get the license, 18 for the FIRST renewal, then 15 CE (8 legal). Do not swap them.
1.5x up to 90 days, 2x up to six months, then a new license.
A power of attorney exempts only up to three transactions a year.
A sales agent cannot act without a sponsoring broker; termination puts the license on inactive status.
The wholesaler exemption needs WRITTEN disclosure of the equitable interest.
vocab: The licensed broker a sales agent acts for and through.
A sales agent license with no sponsoring broker; the agent cannot practice.
Sales Agent Apprentice Education, the 18 hours required for the first renewal.
An option or contract right to buy, which can be assigned with written disclosure.
A person acting under a power of attorney.

tx/special.blurb: Community property, homestead, DTPA, wills, leases, foreclosure, liens.

examples.s: A landlord keeps a $1,200 deposit in bad faith; $800 of it was wrongfully withheld.

tx/special.label: Special topics

check.q: A house inherited by one spouse during marriage is:
Selling a homestead that is one spouse's separate property requires:

l: Texas is a community property state. Community property is what either spouse acquires during marriage, other than separate property.
Separate property: owned or claimed before marriage; acquired during marriage by gift, devise, or descent; and a personal-injury recovery (except lost earning capacity).
Property possessed during marriage is PRESUMED community; separate property must be proved by clear and convincing evidence.
Neither spouse may sell, convey, or encumber the HOMESTEAD without the joinder of the other - even if it is one spouse's separate property.

check.q: A rural homestead for a family may be up to:

l: A homestead is protected from creditors' claims except for purchase money, taxes, written contracts for improvements, refinances, home equity loans and reverse mortgages meeting the Constitution, and owelty of partition.
URBAN homestead: up to 10 acres in one or more contiguous lots.
RURAL homestead: up to 200 acres for a family; up to 100 acres for a single adult.
Proceeds of selling a homestead are protected for six months after the sale.

choices: Exempt from the DTPA as professional opinion
Always a DTPA violation if wrong
check.q: A licensee's honest opinion of value is generally:
check.why: 17.49(c). A misstated fact is not exempt.

sections.h: Deceptive Trade Practices Act (Bus. & Com. Code 17.41 ff.)
l: A consumer may sue for false, misleading, or deceptive acts relied on, breach of warranty, or unconscionable action.
Economic damages; if KNOWING, up to THREE TIMES economic damages plus mental anguish; if intentional, up to three times economic and mental anguish damages.
Professional services advice, judgment or opinion are exempt - but NOT an express misrepresentation of material fact, or a failure to disclose.
Sue within TWO years of the act or its discovery.

check.q: A will entirely in the testator's handwriting:

l: A person of sound mind may make a will if 18 or older, married or formerly married, or in the armed forces.
A will must be in writing, signed, and attested by TWO or more credible witnesses at least 14 years old.
A HOLOGRAPHIC will - wholly in the testator's handwriting - needs no witnesses.

check.q: A security deposit must be refunded within:

l: Refund the security deposit on or before the 30TH DAY after the tenant surrenders the premises, with a written itemized list of deductions.
No deduction for normal wear and tear.
Bad faith retention: $100 + three times the amount wrongfully withheld + attorney's fees. Missing the 30-day deadline presumes bad faith.
A landlord may not lock out a tenant except by judicial process, with narrow exceptions such as repairs, emergencies, or changing locks of a delinquent tenant under the statute's notice rules.

choices: The first Tuesday of the month
The last Friday of the month
check.q: Texas nonjudicial foreclosure sales happen on:

l: Nonjudicial sales under a deed of trust are public auctions at the county courthouse between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. on the FIRST TUESDAY of the month (first Wednesday if Tuesday is Jan 1 or July 4).
Notice of sale at least 21 DAYS before the sale: posted at the courthouse, filed with the county clerk, and sent by certified mail.
For a residence, the servicer must first give at least 20 DAYS to cure the default.

choices: A later buyer for value without notice
check.q: An unrecorded deed is void against:

l: Recording (Property Code 13.001-.002): an unrecorded deed or deed of trust is void against a creditor or later buyer for value WITHOUT NOTICE, but binds the parties, their heirs, and anyone with notice or who paid nothing. Recording gives notice to all.

Mechanic's liens (Property Code 53): an original contractor on a residential project files the lien affidavit by the 15th day of the THIRD month after work is completed. A lien on a homestead needs a written contract signed before work begins, by both spouses if married, and filed with the county clerk.
HOAs (Property Code 207.003): within 10 BUSINESS DAYS of a request, the association delivers the restrictions, bylaws and rules, and a resale certificate.
Veterans Land Board: part of the General Land Office; offers low-interest land and home loans to Texas veterans and military members.

tx/special.summary: Texas law outside the License Act that the exam treats as yours to know: community property and homestead, the DTPA, wills, landlord-tenant, foreclosure, recording, liens, the VLB, HOAs.
traps: Gift, inheritance, and property owned before marriage are separate; everything else acquired during marriage is presumed community.
Homestead: both spouses sign, even if separate property.
Urban 10 acres; rural 200 family, 100 single.
Deposit refund: 30 days; bad faith = $100 + 3x + fees.
Foreclosure: first Tuesday, 10-4, 21 days' notice, 20 days to cure first.
A holographic will needs no witnesses; a typed will needs two aged 14+.
vocab: Property acquired during marriage other than separate property.
Owned before marriage, or received by gift, devise, or descent.
Both spouses signing a conveyance or encumbrance.
Protected residence: 10 urban acres, 200/100 rural acres.
A will wholly in the testator's handwriting.
HOA document of dues, fees and restrictions for a buyer.
A lien to equalize a division of property, allowed on a homestead.
